findings.open_question_chat_affordance_keys: PARTIALLY RESOLVED by PUPPET-308; the KEY half is still open. What this frame settles is structural and is now encoded: rows 1-5 carry a '[ ]'/'[✔]' checkbox marker (note that 'Type something' DOES on a multi-select pane, unlike on question-single) while '6. Chat about this' renders BELOW the horizontal rule with no marker at all. parseQuestionRegion now records that per row and DetectQuestion reports it as InputOption.toggle (true for 1-5, false for 6), which lets chat's writeAnswer stop appending submitKeys (Tab) after a row that closes the dialog — previously answering '6' wrote '6' then Tab, and the Tab landed wherever the dialog left the cursor. STILL NOT EXERCISED: whether the bare digit '6' ACTIVATES that row or merely moves the ❯ highlight onto it (which is what it does on the single-select pane, hence '4\r' there). The keys for row 6 are therefore left UNCHANGED at a bare '6'. Re-open with a live capture: press the chat row's digit on a settled multi-select pane and read the next frame — dialog gone means the digit activates; ❯ moved with the dialog still up means the keys must become '6\r'.

version_note: `claude --version` was re-probed at capture time and reported 2.1.251 (Claude Code) — the version this ticket targets. No discrepancy to record.
trust_note: The recording cwd was `git init`-ed and trust was granted in an EARLIER, discarded session, so the folder-trust dialog does not appear anywhere in this recording. bytes.raw starts at the alt-screen enter (ESC[?1049h) of a clean composer.
teardown_note: bytes.raw is TRUNCATED at the last byte of the settled dialog frame, deliberately, before the Ctrl-] detach teardown. SIGTERM makes claude leave the alt screen (ESC[?1049l) and print 'Resume this session with: claude --resume <id>', and a stream ending there replays as the resume text instead of the dialog. Same trap documented in permission-mode-bypass/meta.json.
expected_note: expected.txt was PRODUCED BY REPLAYING bytes.raw through src/screen's Screen at 120x40 and serializing as screenbench-record does (finalText.replace(/\s+$/u, '') + '\n'). It is not hand-typed.
